number_change_why: The minimal C1 fix changes generated prose and scope/method metadata only. It need not change estimates, CIs, counts, k, trial membership or add numerical results. Denominator: all 32 served HTML pages and their review objects checked; 32 affected, zero clean. Their recorded retrieval classes are 17 TITLE_SEEDED_RETRIEVAL, 11 KNOWN_ITEM_RETRIEVAL and 4 HAND_WRITTEN_KEYWORD_SEARCH. None licenses systematic-search completeness. The instance list contains 75 separate page passages, grouping multiple claims within one resolution paragraph.
fix: At included_tab, replace the static phrase with 'The family-level ledger of recorded eligible trial families and their recorded gaps is in the Screening tab.' At scope.assess, remove the inference that scope differences exclude unretrieved evidence; say that differing scope prevents interpreting the k difference as a retrieval measure. Compute separate P, I, C and O assessments with source evidence and MATCH/MISMATCH/UNKNOWN states; missing evidence must remain UNKNOWN. Population restrictions must be checked individually, not accepted after any population keyword matches. At _comparator and _overview, render those assessments rather than the legacy population_match/scope_valid summary. Add a shared fail-closed policy for completeness prose: absent, non-systematic or conflicting search/search_completeness states cannot authorize it. Do not blindly pass legacy comparator_scope_note claims through this policy. Render a neutral resolution such as 'The comparator has a different scope; search completeness is not established.' Derive comparator method only from its own source-backed method object/text, otherwise display 'Method not established'; never derive network methodology from drug-class scope. Static content: neutral templates and state labels. Dynamic content: recorded search state, per-axis source evidence and comparator method evidence. Numerical analysis stays untouched.
plant: Read-only checks executed against today's actual generators, using r = json.loads(Path('reviews/semaglutide-obesity-mace/review.json').read_text(encoding='utf-8')). All three exact predicates returned False: assert 'not a search gap' not in page._comparator(r, False); assert 'population match: True' not in page._comparator(r, False); assert 'with every eligible trial family' not in review_tabs.included_tab(r). Preserve these as regression tests; each passes after the proposed generator correction. Extend the fixture by deepcopying this served review, setting search.retrieval_class.class = 'KNOWN_ITEM_RETRIEVAL' and search.retrieval_class.label = 'KNOWN-ITEM RETRIEVAL — NOT A SYSTEMATIC SEARCH', leaving its offending resolution note and absent-trial rows intact. Exact additional assertion: assert 'network-level' not in page._comparator(r, False) when comparator_panel[0]['method'] is None. Add an axis-contract assertion after scope computation: assert set(scope_result['axes']) == {'P', 'I', 'C', 'O'}, with unsupported axes explicitly UNKNOWN. Finally parameterize the first three prose assertions over the 32 served review fixtures and verify numerical fields remain identical. No test files were written or modified.
undetermined: The comparator full-text files referenced by the semaglutide MACE, dapagliflozin HFpEF, empagliflozin HFpEF and sacubitril objects are absent from this supplied snapshot; a filename search found no alternative copies. Consequently I cannot independently establish their actual statistical method types or complete source-backed PICO matches. The three 'network-level' passages above are demonstrably configuration-derived and unsupported by populated method fields; I am not claiming to have proved the publications are non-network analyses. Sacubitril's explicit network-meta description could be correct, so I have not counted that description separately as a proven method-inference violation. I cannot establish the true eligible-trial universe or whether SELECT is actually the only eligible trial from these non-systematic searches. I inspected comparator_panel.py: its render function reads its own method fact and renders absence when null; it does not generate the offending network-level wording. No additional served-review instance was attributed to index.py. Explicit incompleteness disclosures, scoped statements about recorded rows, and per-record screening exclusions were not counted as completeness claims. No files were modified; no post-fix execution was possible because this was a read-only review.
